title: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA)
what: The Pazin State Archive holds the parish registers of central Istria. Two letters to this family, of 26 April and 24 June 2021, enclosed the certified copy of Josip Defranceschi's 1863 baptism and prints from the Status Animarum of Gallignana for the households of Antonius and of Giovanni Battista.
cites: MKR župe Gračišće 1841–1899, entry 23 of 1863
Status Animarum, DVD 18, ZM34K 217, M01071656
Status Animarum, DVD 18, ZM34K 217, M01072071
Church books ZM34K-214 and ZM34K-215, Gologorica, Gračišće and Lindar
note: They charge for research and will search, certify and post a named record. The two 2021 requests cost 117 and 124 kuna including overseas postage.

title: Arolsen Archives — International Center on Nazi Persecution
what: The former International Tracing Service. Holds the wartime and displaced-persons records of some seventeen and a half million people, and 79 records under this surname — many more than the family's own copy of file D-1.505. Mined to the bottom in September 2026: the Reutlingen town list of Yugoslav nationals, the wartime sickness-fund cards in their original colour, the IRO care-and-maintenance file, and the whole of displaced-persons folder DP0758 — nineteen French occupation cards for the two brothers' households, holding Petar's photograph, the day Zdravko's family sailed for Australia, and Luise's statelessness.
cites: DP folder DP0758, reference 03010101 05 070 — nineteen cards, IRO 148.901 and 148.902
Counselling card, category CB, 28.4.51, with the entries of 22.7.49, 28.4.51 and 25.5.51
Carte d'identité de personnes déplacées no. 30040, issued 27 November 1946 to Lujza Defranceski
Tracing and documentation case no. 349.822, reference 06030302.0.349.822, 8 documents, 1954–1984 — withheld online
Personal file of DEFRANCESKI, PETAR, CM/1 files from Germany (3.2.1.1), 6 documents
note: Access requires accepting a declaration about sensitive personal data; the account holder must do that himself. Person rows in the search results are click handlers, not links, and the page images sit on a separate server that requires a referer header. The T/D tracing case is the one substantial thing still unread: eight documents spanning 1954 to 1984, withheld online for data protection and obtainable only by written request to Bad Arolsen.

title: Hrvatski državni arhiv
what: The Croatian State Archive. HDA 583 is the Pisino (Pazin) marriage register in which Carlo De Franceschi signs as a witness on 13 September 1842, giving his rank as I. R. Auscultans.
cites: HDA 583, Pisino marriages 1842–43

title: Matične knjige — Croatian parish registers
what: The baptism of Ana Kalanj at Ledenice on 3 January 1864; the baptism of Anton Rudolf at Klenovica on 20 January 1890, which gives the parents' place of origin as Gallignana in Istria; the marriage of Nodburga Defranceschi at Bakar on 27 February 1794.
note: Held as scans by the family.

title: Comune di San Daniele del Friuli and Comune di Concesio — atti di morte
what: Italian civil death registers: Pietro De Franceschi, mason, aged 44, in the civic hospital at San Daniele on 30 March 1895; Edoardo De Franceschi, former officer of Zara, aged 48, in the same hospital on 12 August 1899; Giovanni De Franceschi, aged three, at Concesio above Brescia on 15 July 1916.
cites: San Daniele del Friuli, atti di morte no. 19 (1895) and no. 28 (1899)
Concesio, atti di morte, parte II serie A (1916)

title: Antenati — Portale degli Antenati
what: The Italian state archives' genealogy portal. The Archivio di Stato di Udine has 49,184 registers on it, including 6,693 for the communes of the Tolmezzo tribunal — that is Carnia — and fifty-nine for the Comune di Mione alone. The three De Franceschi birth acts of 1809–1810 at Mione and Muina come from there.
cites: Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1809 e 1810
Nati, indice 1806–1810, sig. 12954
note: Its name search sits behind a bot check, which this archive does not bypass. Browsing the registers by place and year needs no such thing, and the images are served openly over IIIF — which is how these were read.

title: FamilySearch
what: The single largest source in this archive. Its collection «Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994» (cc 2040054) supplied the burial and baptism entries; its persona search supplied the household reconstructions, the emigrant records and the four children of Josip and Ana Kalanj; its catalogue supplied the parish-book inventory.
cites: Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994 (cc 2040054)
note: Free with an account. Only about a quarter of that collection is name-indexed; the rest is images to be read. Nothing was bulk-downloaded.

title: Find a Grave
what: Ninety-six memorials under every spelling of the surname, from which the grave gazetteer is built. Each name on that page links to its own memorial.
note: A volunteer index, heavily weighted to the English-speaking world and Italy. Croatia is almost absent from it, and the count of one Croatian grave is a fact about the index before it is a fact about the family.

title: Wikimedia Commons
what: Four public-domain works reproduced on the namesakes page: Titian's portrait of Andrea de' Franceschi (Detroit Institute of Arts); the Vasari woodcut of Piero della Francesca from the 1648 Vite; Piero's Urbino diptych; and Mariano de Franceschi's Camel Caravan at Rest.
note: Each file is credited and linked on the namesakes page itself.

title: Lee Steiner, Croatia Church Books — mapped
what: A set of Google Earth overlays mapping every Croatian parish register in the FamilySearch collection to its place, with the browse link for each. Used to inventory what survives on film for Crikvenica, Ledenice, Novi Vinodolski, Grižane, Selce, Senj and Fužine.
note: Held in the family's own files as .kmz.

title: Carlo De Franceschi, «L'Istria: note storiche»
what: The family's own historian on his own country: 524 pages, published at Parenzo by Gaetano Coana and dedicated «alla gioventù dell'Istria». Read here end to end in September 2026 from the Internet Archive's scan. It is the source for the Seget estate's chain of owners and the Cretan origin of that branch, for the whole shape of the diocese of Pedena in which Gallignana and Gologorica sat, and for the 1764 roll of colonist families on the Seget lands. It is also, and importantly, silent about Carnia.
cites: p. 363 — the Seghetto and Giuba estate, Cuchich 1604, Valier 1623, and the de Franceschi «emigrata dall'isola di Candia»
p. 363–364, footnote 3 — Giambattista de Franceschi, deputy to the Imperial Council, and the roll of 30 April 1764
p. 484 — the parishes of the diocese of Pedena, and the chapter at Gallignana with its archpriest
p. 173 — the disputed appointment to the pieve of Gallignana, 1324–1335
p. 328–329 — the siege of Gallignana, May 1617
p. 205 — Francesco Claj, priest of Gallignana, and the Croatian translations, 1 January 1563
note: Free and complete online, which the archive had not realised. The OCR text layer is poor — accents garbled, words split at line ends, footnotes badly mangled — so page references above are approximate to the printed pagination shown in the scan, and anyone quoting should open the image.

title: «Lettere di Carlo De Franceschi a Giovanni Kobler»
where: Atti e Memorie della Società Istriana, 1928
what: The letters in which Carlo, about 1873, sets out what his family believed about itself: that it came from Carnia and settled in Istria «intorno al 1700»; that De Franceschi still lived at Mione and Muina; that his trisavolo Giambattista built the 1711 house at Gologorica; and the blazon of the family arms.
note: The single most important narrative source in this archive.

title: Camillo De Franceschi, «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino»
what: Carlo's son on the county the family lived in — still the standard work. With his editions of the Labin statutes, the Piran chartulary and «Gli Artizoni di Parenzo».
note: Some of the primary sources Camillo used were destroyed in the Second World War and its aftermath. For those documents his articles are now the only witness.

title: Blasonario Giuliano
what: The armorial of Venezia Giulia. Its entry «Franceschi (De) — Pisino, Moncalvo, Pola» names Carlo and Camillo and gives the family's arms; a separate entry covers the Seghetto, Capodistria and Umago branch, and others the Capodistria and Ližnjan families.
cites: Blasonario_D.pdf
Blasonario_F.pdf
note: The blazon of the Moncalvo arms is credited to «(C. de F.)» — Carlo himself — with Benedetti and de Totto supplying the tinctures. It formalises his testimony rather than confirming it independently.

title: Petar Puhmajer, «Stancija de Franceschi u Segetu kod Umaga»
what: The conservation monograph on the Seget estate: how it was bought from the Valier in 1720, how the house was built and rebuilt, and the two Istrian branches.

title: «La tenuta de Franceschi di Seghetto», la Voce del popolo
what: The Italian-language daily of Rijeka on the Seget estate: the county in Crete, the 1538 defence of Calus, Lemiores and Sabionera, the shipwreck of 1669, the hundred thousand ducats of 1716, the library of four thousand volumes and its destruction, and the arms on the tympanum. Photographs by Gianfranco Abrami.
note: Where it and the Blasonario disagree on a date, the armorial is preferred and the difference is stated.

title: Deborah Howard, «Titian's Portraits of Grand Chancellor Andrea de' Franceschi»
what: The life of Andrea de' Franceschi, born 1473, Grand Chancellor of Venice from 15 September 1529 until his death in 1552, buried at Santi Giovanni e Paolo — his embassies, his will and its five codicils, and the Titian portraits he left his nephew.

title: Josip Banić, «Venetian Istria in the Embrace of a Nascent Dominium (c. 1381 – c. 1470)»
what: A modern historian's verdict on Camillo: one of three figures who «tower» over Istrian medieval studies, and the only surviving witness to sources lost in the war. Quotes Egidio Ivetic that for medieval Istria one must rely on Benussi, Carlo De Franceschi and De Vergottini.

title: Centro di Ricerche Storiche di Rovigno — catalogue of Istrian sacred art
what: Catalogues the paintings in the chapel of Stancija Seghetto — formerly Villa De Franceschi — and records their poor condition; and a Pentecost whose patron Antonio Alisi identified as «un de Franceschi nobile di Seghetto».

title: Hrvatski plemićki zbor — the Franceschi family
what: The Croatian Noble Corps on the Zadar and Omiš descent: Niccolò received into the Hungarian-Croatian nobility by charter at Buda in 1359; the branch at Omiš from Francesca de Franceschi in the later sixteenth century; Giovanni «il Zuane» and the siege of Imotski in 1718.

title: Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani
what: The biographies of Carlo De Franceschi, Camillo De Franceschi and Girolamo de' Franceschi of Koper, bishop of Corone.

title: Diocesan and press notices for Mons. Lucio Soravito de Franceschi
where: Arcidiocesi di Udine; Cathopedia; Messaggero Veneto
what: Born at Mione di Ovaro on 8 December 1939, ordained 1963, Bishop of Adria-Rovigo 2004–2015, died 6 July 2019. The evidence that the surname was still in the village of the 1679 headmen's list two hundred and sixty years later.

title: «The DeFranceschi Family Tree Album»
where: printed for the first family reunion, Crystal Springs Resort, 7–9 September 2012
what: The American branch's own history and chart, headed «started by Antonio DeFranceschi 8/6/1856 – 10/23/1924 + Maria Valhart 4/6/1867 – 1945». Eleven children, five countries. Also the description of the arms carved on the 1711 house at Moncalvo.
note: Assembled from Anton Rumac's handwritten notes and a cassette tape made by cousin Bruno. Its compiler says plainly there will be errors; where it can be checked against registers, it holds.

title: The family's MacFamilyTree file
what: A database of 281 people and 247 photographs, catalogued and captioned by the family. The source of every portrait on this site of the Crikvenica house, and of the photographs of three graves.
note: Where it conflicts with a register — Zdravko's death year, Josip's wife — the register is preferred and the conflict is stated on the page.

title: defranceski.com
what: The roster of significant persons, the account of the four Croatian lines, the collected blazons, and the descent chart that first set out the line from Giovanni of Gologorica to Brisbane.
note: This archive absorbs its content rather than duplicating it; its hosted images are token-gated and could not be fetched, so equivalent public-domain works were sourced from Wikimedia Commons instead.

title: The Omiš and Seget photographs
what: Studio portraits of the Omiš branch — Josip and Anna with baby Ante, Zane, Frane, Anton «Toni» of 1932 — and seven photographs of the Seget villa: the 1843 façade, the tympanum with its carved arms, the crenellated tower, the rustic range and the well.

title: MyHeritage family tree export, July 2018
what: A GEDCOM of 8,286 individuals, 254 of them carrying this surname, compiled by the family on MyHeritage and grown by that site's Smart Matching and by Geni's SmartCopy through 2017. Two very different things are inside it. Its Crikvenica and Blažević entries are first-hand family knowledge — dates off gravestones and the backs of photographs — and they are the archive's only source for nine of the people on this site, including Anton's birth at Reutlingen on 22 August 1944. Its Dalmatian and Venetian upper reaches are a compiled noble pedigree with no register citations, and it joins that pedigree to this family in error.
cites: Anton Defranceski, b. 22 August 1944 Reutlingen, d. 28 June 1999 Ipswich
Ruža Hreljac, b. 13 February 1922 Fužine, d. 30 January 1996 Horsham
Hedviga Blažević, b. 8 March 1926 Senj, d. 30 October 2001 Johannesburg
Ivan Defranceski, b. 25 June 1925 Crikvenica, d. 30 October 1995 Senj
Josip «Pepe» Defranceski 1911–1980 and Božica Blašković 1911–1994
note: Read with care and read to the bottom. The seam where the two families are joined is set out on the Imotski page; below it the file is the best source the archive has for the twentieth-century household. Its narrative notes on the Imotski family are quoted from stariimotski.com, credited there to the archive of Captain Vjeko Franceschi.

title: Geneanet — «Urban ANTOINE's Family Tree», published by the member «carnia»
what: A Carnian researcher's tree covering the villages of the Gorto valley. It holds the only rounded De Franceschi household this archive has for Mione — five generations of the «dal Ginut» house, with trades, house-names, burial at the Pieve di Gorto, and notes written in Carnian Friulian rather than Italian. Its dates are register-precise and internally consistent, which for an online tree is unusual and suggests direct work in the Ovaro books.
cites: Francesco Arcangelo De Franceschi, «Checo dal Ginut», 5 Aug 1852 – 9 Jun 1939, tessitore contadino
Leopoldo Eugenio De Franceschi, «Poldo dal Ginut», 15 Sep 1900 – 30 Sep 1973, marangon boscador
GioBatta De Franceschi, 16 Jun 1816 – Aug 1906, and Anna Lucia Giorgis, 20 Nov 1820 – 3 Dec 1852
Maddalena Erman, daughter of Benedetto Erman, in the Giorgis ancestry
note: Two saved pages are in the family's own files; the tree itself is behind a Geneanet login and parts need a premium account. No descent from this household to the Istrian line is claimed or shown. The member is worth writing to.

title: istrianet.org — Carlo De Franceschi, «L'Istria», transcribed
where: Held in the family's files since November 2004 as «Defranceski History.doc»
what: A clean transcription of several chapters of Carlo's 1879 book, made from the Arnaldo Forni reprint, with maps from Egidio Ivetic's «L'Istria moderna» and biography from Benussi — both Centro di Ricerche Storiche, Rovigno. It covers the depopulation of Istria by war and plague and the repopulation by colonists, and it carries the Seget passage and the roll of 30 April 1764 in readable text.
cites: The Cuchich investiture of 1604, the Valier sale of 1623 and the de Franceschi purchase «emigrata dall'isola di Candia»
«Addì 30 Aprile 1764 Seghetto di Umago» — the roll of colonist families, corrected against this text
note: The file had been in the family's own folders for twenty-two years, unopened by this project until September 2026. It is a web capture, not a manuscript, and it is Carlo's published book rather than any family history — but it is a better text than the OCR, and the archive's transcription of the 1764 roll has been corrected from it.

title: The family's own copy of the Reutlingen displaced-persons file
what: The French-zone and IRO papers for both brothers' households, photographed by the family. It overlaps Arolsen's online folder DP0758 in part — but it also holds what Arolsen does not: the whole of Zdravko, Ruža and Anton's file, whose Arolsen index card is stamped «CM/1 destroyed». Zdravko's fiche carries his photograph; Ruža's carries a photograph of her holding the baby. It also holds two documents that change the reading of the file: the IRO director's letter of 27 May 1949 explaining the B and BJ classifications, and a health-service slip recording that Petar was screened for Brazil.
cites: A. Poignant, Director of the IRO French zone, to the Chef de Service du Wurtemberg, 27 May 1949 — «Cas de DEFRANCESKI (148.902)»
Dr S. Birietaité, Chef de Service de Santé — «passé au screening — Brésil. Rien à signaler»
Fiches individuelles 30560 (Zdravko), 30561 (Ruža), 52852 (Anton), 52850 (Ursula), 52851 (Renate), 30609 (Petar)
Identity cards of 27 November 1946, each annotated later «8/3/1949 Australie»
Stadt Reutlingen certificates of 28 February 1950 for Anton, Felix, Ivan, Zdravko and Ruža
note: Read in September 2026, after sitting unopened in the project's own folder list. Where it and the Arolsen index disagree — Ruža's birth date — three documents here agree on 13 February 1922 against Arolsen's single 2 May.

title: Anita Marin, «Oznake vlasništva i posvete na knjigama Knjižnice obitelji De Franceschi»
what: The paper that told this archive its subject's library still exists. Written by the librarian of the Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica in Zagreb who catalogued the collection. It establishes that the books and family archive of the De Franceschi of Gologorica reached the NSK after 1945, stood unprocessed for over fifty years, and now hold 2,480 catalogued items under the shelfmark PDF — Poklon De Franceschi — together with fourteen boxes and seven folders of family archive containing Carlo's and Camillo's manuscript drafts, the family correspondence, estate papers, photographs and an album.
cites: 2,480 items: 138 serials and 2,341 monographs, 1503–1945
«pronađena izbačena iz ormara i razbacana po kući» — found in 1945 thrown out of the cupboards and scattered about the house
Giulio De Franceschi, painter, Rijeka 1856 – Gologorica 1942
Seventeen stamped ex libris of Tomaso Luciani (Labin 1818 – Venice 1894)
217 of 2,341 books carry any ownership mark — the family used signatures, never a bookplate
note: Open access and free. The ResearchGate copy is behind a bot check; the journal's own PDF at morepress.unizd.hr is not. In Croatian, with an English abstract.

title: Marin, Jurišić & Matijaca, «Arhiv obitelji De Franceschi u Nacionalnoj i sveučilišnoj knjižnici u Zagrebu»
what: The published inventory of the family archive, shelfmark PDF 2.337 — fourteen boxes and nine folders, described box by box by the three librarians who arranged them. It is the document this archive was about to write to Zagreb to ask for. Among what it lists: the household accounts of Gologorica for 1925–26 and 1929–30; a lease of the second floor of the house to the parish priest in 1907; the photograph album; five boxes of correspondence including Carlo's «Lettere archeologiche a Pietro Kandler»; the personal papers of Carlo, Camillo, Gian Pietro and Giulio; and the architect's plan of the family chapel in the cemetery at Gologorica.
cites: Shelfmark PDF 2.337 — 14 boxes and 9 folders, material from the 18th century to 1943
Box 6 — the photograph album, and «Maria De Franceschi, Parenzo, 187[?]»
Boxes 7–11 — «Lettere archeologiche a Pietro Kandler»; Camillo to his sister Faustina, 1886–1893
Box 12 — «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino», by the architect Giuseppe Hirsch
Folder 6 — «Nelle fauste occasioni delle nozze Maria De Franceschi — Luigi Salamon, Pola, 25 ottobre 1897»
note: Open access at ojs.srce.hr. Croatian, with an English abstract. Found through Crossref after ResearchGate refused this session.

title: Jakov Jelinčić, «Korespondencija Giovanni Kobler — Carlo De Franceschi», I–III
where: Vjesnik historijskih arhiva u Rijeci i Pazinu XXI (1977), XXII (1978), and part III
what: Kobler's side of the correspondence — the letters Carlo was answering — edited and published in three parts. Sixteen years of letters between two men who, Jelinčić notes, never managed to meet. It contains Kobler's inventory of the Defranceschi households of Fiume, his question «È forse Lei un Discendente?», and the record of Valentino Defranceschi, come from Carnia and made a citizen of Fiume in 1739.
cites: Valentino Defranceschi, «venuto dalla Carnia», citizen of Fiume 1739; the Chapel of St Helen, 1764; his tomb in the Duomo, epigraph 1785
Giovanni Antonio De Franceschi, doctor of law and municipal chancellor, d. 1727
Giovanni Battista Defranceschi, come from the County of Pisino about 1740
note: Open access on Hrčak, free. Italian letters with a Croatian editorial apparatus.

title: Stipan Trogrlić, «Gologorica u Kronici Župe (1892.–1918.) prema zapisima župnika Ljudevita Žvačeka»
what: The parish chronicle of Gologorica for 1892–1918, as kept by the parish priest Ljudevit Žváček — on the national-political, moral-religious, economic-social and ethnographic life of the village. Žváček is the same priest to whom Giulio and Camillo de Franceschi let the second floor of their house in 1907. Croatian, with Italian and English versions of the article.
note: Open access on Hrčak. Not yet read in detail by this archive.

title: Hrčak — the portal of Croatian scientific and professional journals
what: Free, open, and the place where Croatian scholarship on this family actually lives. A search for «De Franceschi» returns twenty-three items including the three NSK collection papers, the Kobler correspondence in three parts, and reviews of Camillo's history of the County of Pazin in its 2023 Croatian translation. «Gologorica» returns seven, «Gračišće» thirteen — among them the parish chronicle, the urban development of the town, the altar of the Madonna of Mercy, and the last Habsburg emperor's visit on 6 April 1918.
note: Search «De Franceschi» with the space, not «Defranceschi» — the fused spelling returns mostly Croatian rheumatology papers by an unrelated co-author. Hrčak was reachable directly where ResearchGate, Geneanet and WikiTree all served this session a bot check.

title: Miroslav Bertoša, «Gologorički De Franceschi: između etosa i etnosa»
where: in «Etos i etnos zavičaja», Čakavski sabor, Pula – Rijeka 1985, pp. 177–253
what: Seventy-six pages on the De Franceschi of Gologorica by one of Croatia's leading historians of Istria — «between ethos and ethnos», on a family that was Friulian-Carnian in origin and Italian-national in politics, in a village that was Croatian in speech. It is the standing scholarly account of the household this archive's Gologorica registers reconstruct, and it is the source Trogrlić leans on for the statement that the family settled there in the seventeenth century.
cites: «furlansko-karnijske obitelji De Franceschi, koja se naselila u Gologoricu još u 17. st.» — quoted by Trogrlić
note: Not yet read by this archive. It is a 1985 book chapter and not online; it would have to come from a Croatian library or by interlibrary loan. On the evidence of what quotes from it, it is the most important single thing still unread.

title: Irma Huić, «Urbanistički razvoj Gračišća u Istri»
where: Prostor 23 (2015) 2, pp. 208–221 — Faculty of Architecture, University of Zagreb
what: The first study anyone has made of how Gračišće grew — the family's own parish. It locates the bishop of Pedena's palace in the village, and the Salamon palace built facing it; and its source list points at the Franciscan cadastre of Gallignana of about 1820 at Trieste, and at the published urbaria of the County of Pazin of 1498 and the sixteenth century.
cites: «Gotovo istovremeno nasuprot biskupskoj rezidenciji gradi se palača Salamon»
ASTr, Catasto franceschino, Distretto di Pisino, Comune di Gallignana d'Istria, foglio IV sezione IV
note: Open access on Hrčak. Its Franceschi citations are all to Carlo's book of 1879 and Camillo's of 1964.

title: ANNO — Historische Zeitungen und Zeitschriften, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek
what: Full-text searchable historic Austrian newspapers, free and without registration. Istria was Austrian until 1918, so the Istrian press is in it. A search for «Defranceschi» returns 722 issues — heavily «Il Giornaletto di Pola» of 1914–15, «Naša Sloga» of Trieste and Pula, and a «Bozner Zeitung» of 1876. Narrowing to «"De Franceschi" Gallignana» returns eight, in «Il giovine Pensiero» of Pola between 1893 and 1897 and «Il Popolo Istriano» of 1898 and 1901 — the surname and the family's own parish named in the same issue.
cites: 722 issues on «Defranceschi»
8 issues pairing «De Franceschi» with Gallignana, 1893–1901
note: Opened in September 2026 and not yet harvested. The search is an Angular application with no usable public API found; it has to be worked through the interface. Narrow queries first — the bare surname returns too much, and much of the Pola material of 1914–15 will be unrelated bearers of the name.

title: The State Archives of Friuli Venezia Giulia — Trieste, Udine, Gorizia, Pordenone
what: A guide to what each holds. Two things in it bear directly on this archive. The Archivio di Stato di Trieste holds the Austro-Hungarian military records — Trieste recruitment lists, navy recruitment lists and draft cards with service records — and the civil registers of the province for 1924–44 including the municipalities ceded to Yugoslavia in 1947. The Archivio di Stato di Udine holds the «Ruolo della Popolazione», the population rolls of 1836 and 1865, which give for each household the head, the parents' names, religion, date and place of birth and date of marriage — for the province that contains Mione and Ovaro.
cites: Ruolo della Popolazione, Udine province, 1836 and 1865
ASTr — Austro-Hungarian military and navy recruitment lists and draft cards
Archivio di Stato di Gorizia — Libri dei fuochi (household registers) 1830–1956, and Ventilazioni ereditarie 1755–1850
note: Data-protected records open after 75 years unless you are directly related. The state archives do not issue civil certificates. Found through a resource list the family supplied.

title: sortedbyname.com — DEFRANCESCHI
what: 127 entries drawn from the Social Security NUMIDENT and death files, state marriage and death indexes released through ReclaimTheRecords, and Ellis Island passenger manifests. Three American clusters: an Istrian one in New York, a Friulian one at Torrington and Waterbury in Connecticut, and a coal-country one in Harrison County, West Virginia. The New York group includes Basilio Defranceschi and his son Dario, born at Gallignana in 1937 — the first family this archive can trace from Gračišće to America.
cites: Dario Defranceschi, b. 26 September 1937 at Gallignana, son of Basilio and Maria L. Rovina, d. 29 January 1991
Basilio Defranceschi, b. 29 September 1909, d. 15 June 1994, New York
Joseph Defranceschi, b. 12 March 1892 at Trieste, son of Anthony and Makia Valhart
note: Free. Cloudflare-protected against plain fetching; it loads normally in a browser. No page exists for the Defranceski spelling.

title: dLib.si — the Digital Library of Slovenia
what: Free and open, and it holds runs of the Austrian Littoral periodicals — including Kandler's «L'Istria» of 1846–52, which Irma Huić cites for Gračišće. A surname search returns Slovenian notices of the family's scholarship: Camillo's «Chartularium Piranense», his «I castelli della Val d'Arsa», and a review of Carlo's history of Istria.
note: Reached without a bot check. Its value here is the periodicals rather than the notices; L'Istria has not yet been read for this family.
